items.trail: Great Square represents body of the horse while other lines of stars represent its neck, head and legs

image.alt: Graphic illustration of the Pegasus constellation

items.title: Country diary: Jackdaws carve up the sky as dusk descends on the moors
items.trail: Eldwick Crag, West Yorkshire: In the low light and the high wind, these corvids are preparing to roost for the night. And they seem to be enjoying themselves

image.alt: A dirt track runs along a fenced West Yorkshire moorland ridge under a pale dusk sky
image.caption: The moorland at dusk in West Yorkshire.

items.title: The Pianist review – Władysław Szpilman’s Holocaust memoir retold with his own music
items.trail: This adaptation is perhaps too smooth but is well-staged and performed, and draws strong feeling from the pianist’s compositions

image.alt: complex image. The ghost of Szpilman seen from behind at an upright piano. In the background, two string players at ground level and Szpilman and Janina elevate
image.caption: Chamber piece … Daniel Krikler as the Polish pianist Władysław Szpilman and Mischa Jardine as Janina in The Pianist.

items.title: ‘Nothing worked for me until I was clean and sober’: Ashley Walters on acting, directing – and turning his life around
items.trail: In Adolescence he proved himself one of the UK’s best actors. Now he has directed his first film, Animol. He reflects on the road from prison and addiction to soaring success

image.alt: Portrait of Ashley Walters in a black jacket
image.caption: ‘I’ve got eight kids, three grandkids, I’m paying a mortgage!’ … Ashley Walters.

items.title: Adultery review – a risible tale of middle-aged car sex, rat poo and rickety furniture
items.trail: Romola Garai and Dominic Cooper are far too good for this by-the-numbers tale of two people having an affair. It is a clattering bag of cliches

image.alt: Hannah and Beth stand back to back in a bar, one with arms crossed looking sideways
image.caption: Giving it everything … Shelley Conn and Romola Garai in Adultery on ITVX.

items.title: This City Is Ours review – the Liverpudlian gang drama is back … and the acting’s as terrific as ever
items.trail: Nefarious doings, tiny-headed henchmen and sockless villains – the mob saga is back. And it’s as lovable as it is bloody

image.alt: A man in a jacket stands outdoors at night in This City Is Ours, bathed in blue light
image.caption: Fun in the sun … Michael (James Nelson-Joyce) in This City Is Ours.

items.title: A Course Called Ireland review – why did Bill Murray ever agree to this Irish golf show?
items.trail: The Hollywood star is so grumpy in this new travelogue it’s like he wishes he wasn’t there. Think sulky car journeys, strained encounters and the sense of a TV series imploding

image.alt: Bill Murray in a green bobble hat and blue jacket looks off to the side outdoors
image.caption: Largely uncommunicative … Bill Murray in A Course Called Ireland.
